2607.19935.title: MOF-Sleuth: Tool-Grounded Reward Alignment for Explainable Fine-Grained MOF CIF Auditing
2607.19935.paper_summary: Large metal-organic framework (MOF) databases support simulation, screening, and machine learning through crystallographic information files (CIFs). Subtle chemical and structural errors in these inputs can compromise downstream results and hinder manual inspection. LLM advances in computational chemistry offer paths beyond predictive screening toward fine-grained diagnosis with evidence-grounded explanations. However, two challenges remain: (i) limited fine-grained attribution: MOF-specific validators and machine-learning models scale detection but provide fixed checks, readiness scores, or coarse labels rather than evidence-grounded explanations; and (ii) unreliable CIF reasoning: direct LLM auditing is costly and unreliable because chemical evidence is implicit across atom-site records and requires geometric, connectivity, occupancy, and charge calculations. Both stem from weak coupling between chemical evidence and language-model explanation. We introduce MOF-Sleuth, a reinforcement-guided CIF auditing agent with two modules: a deterministic Forensic Lab and a Sleuth reasoning engine. The Lab derives composition, geometry, connectivity, occupancy, coordination, and charge evidence, and Sleuth uses this evidence to produce an evidence-grounded explanation, error types, and a binary decision. Reward-guided reinforcement learning (RL) turns tool measurements into chemical explanation-level supervision, rewarding not only the final answer but also cited chemical evidence and evidence-supported diagnoses. We introduce Chemically Grounded Diagnosis (Chem-GD), a metric that assesses whether a correct diagnosis is explained by factual, relevant CIF-derived evidence. Across four benchmarks, MOF-Sleuth establishes state-of-the-art performance among LLM-based approaches and MOF-specific machine-learning methods, demonstrating gains in detection, attribution, and grounded explanation quality.
2607.19935.paper_summary_zh: 大型金屬有機框架 (MOF) 數據庫透過結晶學信息文件 (CIF) 支持模擬、篩選和機器學習。這些輸入中的微小化學和結構錯誤可能會影響下游結果並妨礙手動檢查。計算化學中大型語言模型 (LLM) 的進展提供了超越預測篩選的途徑，朝向細緻的診斷和基於證據的解釋。然而，仍然存在兩個挑戰：(i) 有限的細緻歸因：特定於 MOF 的驗證器和機器學習模型擴展了檢測，但提供的是固定的檢查、準備分數或粗略標籤，而不是基於證據的解釋；(ii) 不可靠的 CIF 推理：直接的 LLM 審核成本高且不可靠，因為化學證據在原子位置記錄中是隱含的，並且需要幾何、連接性、佔據和電荷計算。這兩者都源於化學證據與語言模型解釋之間的弱耦合。我們介紹了 MOF-Sleuth，一個增強指導的 CIF 審核代理，具有兩個模塊：一個確定性法醫實驗室和一個 Sleuth 推理引擎。該實驗室推導出組成、幾何、連接性、佔據、配位和電荷證據，而 Sleuth 使用這些證據生成基於證據的解釋、錯誤類型和二元決策。獎勵指導的增強學習 (RL) 將工具測量轉化為化學解釋級別的監督，不僅獎勵最終答案，還獎勵引用的化學證據和基於證據的診斷。我們介紹了化學基礎診斷 (Chem-GD)，這是一個評估正確診斷是否由事實、相關的 CIF 衍生證據解釋的指標。在四個基準測試中，MOF-Sleuth 在基於 LLM 的方法和特定於 MOF 的機器學習方法中建立了最先進的性能，顯示出在檢測、歸因和基於證據的解釋質量方面的提升。
